vocabulary.termEs: Representar en el plano de coordenadas
vocabulary.definition: Plot a point by moving horizontally to its x-coordinate and vertically to its y-coordinate.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Ubicar un punto moviéndose horizontalmente hasta su coordenada x y verticalmente hasta su coordenada y.
vocabulary.cloze: Plot a point by moving to its ___-coordinate first, then its ___-coordinate.

examples.why: The x move comes first, always.

vocabulary.definition: A grid with a line going across and a line going up to plot points.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cuadrícula con una línea horizontal y una vertical para marcar puntos.
vocabulary.visual: A grid with a horizontal line (x-axis) crossing a vertical line (y-axis), making four sections
vocabulary.cloze: The grid made by a horizontal and a vertical number line is the ___.

examples.text: A grid with an x-axis and a y-axis crossing at 0
examples.why: Two number lines that let a pair name one point.
One line can place a number, but not a pair.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers (x, y) that tell where a point is on a grid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos números (x, y) que dicen dónde está un punto en una cuadrícula.
vocabulary.visual: (3, 5) means move right 3 from the origin, then up 5
vocabulary.cloze: Two numbers (x, y) that tell the location of a point are an ___.

examples.why: The order tells you across first, then up.
Swapping the numbers lands somewhere else entirely.

vocabulary.definition: The point (0, 0) where the two grid lines cross.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El punto (0, 0) donde se cruzan las dos líneas de la cuadrícula.
vocabulary.visual: The starting point at the center where both axes cross — (0, 0)
vocabulary.cloze: The point (0, 0) where the x-axis and y-axis cross is the ___.

examples.why: Both coordinates are zero — the starting point.
It sits on the y-axis, five units up from the origin.

vocabulary.definition: One of the four parts of a coordinate grid, numbered I to IV.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una de las cuatro partes de una cuadrícula de coordenadas, numeradas I a IV.
vocabulary.visual: I (+,+) top-right, II (-,+) top-left, III (-,-) bottom-left, IV (+,-) bottom-right
vocabulary.cloze: One of the four regions of the coordinate plane is a ___.

examples.why: Negative x and positive y put it up and to the left.
A point on an axis is in no quadrant at all.

vocabulary.definition: A flipped, mirror image across a line.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una imagen reflejada al otro lado de una línea.
vocabulary.visual: (3, 2) reflected over the x-axis becomes (3, -2) — same x, opposite y
vocabulary.cloze: A flip of a point or shape over an axis is a ___.

examples.why: The axis you flip over keeps its coordinate; the other flips sign.
That flipped x — a reflection across the y-axis instead.

vocabulary.definition: Whole numbers and their opposites, like -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números enteros y sus opuestos, como -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
vocabulary.cloze: A whole number or its opposite, with no fraction part, is an ___.

examples.why: It is a whole number's opposite with no fraction.
It has a fraction part, so it is not an integer.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Captain Vega’s Treasure Square
revealWordProblem.text: Captain Vega buried treasure at the four corners of a square. Three corners are at (2, 2), (2, 6), and (6, 6). She always plots her corners in Quadrant I. What ordered pair is the fourth corner, and what is the side length of the square?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A blank coordinate plane with x- and y-axes and a grid, for plotting points.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The fourth corner is (6, 2). The square has a side length of 4 units, because from (2, 2) to (6, 2) is 6 − 2 = 4 units and from (2, 2) to (2, 6) is 6 − 2 = 4 units.

reviewCheck.stem: Which ordered pair names a point 3 units right and 7 units up from the origin?
reviewCheck.explanation: The first coordinate is horizontal (right 3), the second is vertical (up 7). So (3, 7).
choiceFeedback: You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.
Remember the x-coordinate tells you how far horizontally.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
hints: Re-read the moves: 3 units right, then 7 units up. Which move comes first in an ordered pair?
An ordered pair is (x, y): x is the right/left distance, y is the up/down distance. Match each move to its slot.
Start at the origin and go right 3 — that 3 is the x, the first number. Now decide where the 'up 7' goes.
reviewCheck.stemEs: ¿Qué par ordenado nombra un punto que está 3 unidades a la derecha y 7 unidades hacia arriba desde el origen?
reviewCheck.explanationEs: La primera coordenada es horizontal (3 a la derecha) y la segunda es vertical (7 hacia arriba). Entonces (3, 7).
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer los movimientos: 3 unidades a la derecha y luego 7 unidades hacia arriba. ¿Cuál movimiento va primero en un par ordenado?
Un par ordenado es (x, y): x es la distancia derecha/izquierda y y es la distancia arriba/abajo. Une cada movimiento con su lugar.
Empieza en el origen y ve 3 a la derecha: ese 3 es la x, el primer número. Ahora decide dónde va el 'arriba 7'.
